legs.label: PHI -1
legs.why: Philadelphia's defense generated a 50% pressure rate in Week 1 and now faces a Titans QB (Ward) coming off a 4.4 YPA, 3-sack dud behind a line missing its projected starting center, while Tennessee's retooled 4-3 defense is a bad matchup for Goedert and Barkley behind an Eagles O-line replacing Dickerson. That combination supports laying the number, while both teams' offensive inefficiency in Week 1 argues for the Under.

legs.label: JAX +8.5
legs.why: Jacksonville looked like the far more complete team in Week 1 (5 sacks, 2 takeaways, 4-TD Lawrence outing) while Denver's offensive line was overwhelmed and the offense was sloppy (3 fumbles, 7 penalties) even in a get-right home spot; that gap plus Denver's own banged-up front five leans toward the Jaguars covering a small home number. The total lean is a lighter conviction Under: Denver's pass rush is a legitimately bad matchup for a shaky Broncos O-line's tempo, though Waddle's integration and Jacksonville's hot start could push it back over.

legs.label: Over 39.5 CIN@HOU
legs.why: Both defenses enter thinned at a key spot — Houston's linebacker corps and Cincinnati's edge (Shemar Stewart out again) — while both offenses showed real juice in Week 1. Houston's pass-rush duo still gives it a slight defensive edge at home, so we lean the Texans on a mild conviction rather than a strong side play; the total lean is stronger given the injury-thinned coverage/pass-rush depth on both sides and each team's proven ability to move the ball.

legs.label: Over 40.5 IND@KC
legs.why: KC's offense faces a Colts defense that just allowed 41 points and struggled versus both the run and explosive pass plays, while Indianapolis's offense gets a Chiefs secondary that traded McDuffie, lost Watson/Cook in free agency, and plays Week 2 without CB Mansoor Delane. That mismatch supports a comfortable Chiefs cover and a game that clears the total. Confidence sits at a moderate 3/5 on each side because Indy gets a full week to self-scout its Week 1 issues and KC's own O-line/red-zone execution was inconsistent versus Denver.

legs.label: SEA +2.5
legs.why: Seattle's defense forced three fourth-quarter picks off Drake Maye in the opener and allowed the fewest points in the league last season, and it should feast on an Arizona offensive line missing starting guard Isaiah Adams; conversely, Arizona's own DT room is down two players to IR, which should let Seattle's run-committee and Drew Lock operate efficiently without needing to force throws downfield. Confidence is capped at 3/5 given the QB downgrade and conflicting expert models (SportsLine likes Seattle -4.5 at 65%; Covers likes the Arizona points).

legs.label: Under 41.5 PIT@NE
legs.why: Both defenses were the story of Week 1 — Pittsburgh forced five takeaways and allowed a top-5 EPA/play mark, while New England allowed a top-8 EPA/play mark. Neither offense showed explosive-play efficiency, and the total has already drifted down from 43.5 to as low as 41.5 across books. Pittsburgh's defensive front (Watt, Highsmith) against a Patriots line that allowed 47 sacks last season should keep New England's drives short even at home, while Pittsburgh's own O-line issues cap their ceiling too — hence Under 42.5. New England is the better overall roster and stays the play to win outright, but a 5.5-point home number is generous against a defense playing at this level, especially with A.J. Brown out; lean the Steelers to keep it within a score.

legs.label: Over 47.5 MIN@CHI
legs.why: The line moved from CHI -3.5/45.5 to -5.5/49.5 purely on Chicago's 59-point explosion against a weak Panthers defense, while Minnesota's own 39-point, 17-point win at Green Bay (with a backup QB for three-plus quarters) is being undervalued; take the extra points with Minnesota given Flores' 82%-blitz-rate defense and a Bears O-line missing RT Trapilo, but only at low-moderate confidence given the Murray uncertainty. The total lean is Over: both offenses are hyper-efficient in the red zone and both defenses are shorthanded, so game script points to another 45+ combined-point affair even if the final margin tightens.

legs.label: Over 41.5 CLE@TB
legs.why: TB is the more talented, more efficient team and CLE's defense was gutted by season-ending injuries in Week 1, supporting a comfortable Bucs win — but TB is 0-10 ATS over its last 10 games and lost 3 fumbles in Week 1, so confidence on laying 8.5 is capped at a light lean rather than a strong one. The total leans Over because both defenses were carved up in Week 1 (CLE allowed 34, TB allowed 33) and neither pass rush has shown it can create consistent pressure yet, though CLE's offensive inefficiency (1-of-8 red zone conversions Week 1) tempers full confidence in a shootout.

legs.label: Over 46.5 NO@BAL
legs.why: Baltimore is the far more talented, healthier roster under a new staff that just dismantled Indianapolis in a three-phase performance, while New Orleans is mid-rebuild on defense (28th in DL talent) and just let a plodding Lions run game post 5.4 YPC. That supports BAL -8.5 covering, though only moderate confidence given Shough proved capable of 410 yards and rallying from three scores down. The total lean is Over: both offenses scored freely in Week 1 against defenses that project as replacement-level, and market total movement toward 47.5-48.5 at other books suggests sharp money agrees the number should be higher.

legs.label: CAR -2.5
legs.why: Carolina gets the lean because Atlanta is starting its third-string QB (Cooper Rush, 2 INT in Wk1) behind a banged-up line (Bergeron out, Lindstrom/Harrison/Dorlus questionable), while Bryce Young just authored a 361-yard, 3-TD outing and Carolina's defensive investment (Phillips, Lloyd, Rozeboom) should eventually show even after a rough Wk1. The total lean is softer: CAR's defense allowing 59 points to Chicago argues for Over, but Rush's limited passing ceiling and ATL's shaky O-line make sustained scoring drives harder to trust, and the market itself has already drifted the total down half a point to 43.5, which aligns with a modest Under lean.

legs.label: Under 50.5 WSH@DAL
legs.why: Dallas's defense posted the league's worst EPA/drive mark in Week 1 with a shorthanded secondary, but Washington's own blitz-heavy defense and a shorthanded Dallas O-line could keep this closer and lower-scoring than the market's 50.5/DAL-3.5 line suggests, especially with both offenses opening slowly. We lean the home dog price and a modest Under, both at low-moderate confidence.
